SCIM cannot adopt existing local accounts or change privileged accounts.
Duplicates return `409` with `scimType: uniqueness`. `DELETE` revokes sessions,
disables the account and hides it from SCIM, keeping its audit and team history;
deleted identifiers and emails are not reused. Requests are limited to 64 KiB
and 100 PATCH operations. The contract follows
[OpenID Connect Core](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html),
[RFC 7643](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7643.html) and
[RFC 7644](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7644.html).

### Verify and recover

1. Confirm local owner sign-in.
2. Provision a test Member through SCIM, sign in through OIDC, and confirm that
   access appears only after team assignment.
3. Deactivate it through SCIM and confirm that its open session loses access.
4. Check the audit log for provisioning, linking, sign-in and deactivation.

If the provider is unavailable, use password sign-in. To turn identity
integration off, clear the OIDC and SCIM variables and restart the admin
service; local accounts, sessions and identity records stay. Disable affected
accounts if their sessions must end too.

## Self-registration

Owners open **Users & roles → Registration allowlist**, add allowed email
domains or addresses (one per line, up to 100 per list) and enable
self-registration. It starts disabled with empty lists, and empty lists admit
nobody. `example.org` and `@example.org` both allow that exact domain;
subdomains are listed separately. Matching is case-insensitive.

Email registration needs SMTP:

1. Set `REVIEW_AGENT_EMAIL_SECRET_KEY` in the console's deployment secrets and
   restart the console once, before saving an SMTP password. Generate the key
   with the command below and back it up separately from the database.

   ```sh
   python -c 'from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())'
   ```

2. As an owner, open **Settings → Email delivery (SMTP)** and enter the server,
   port, sender and optional username and password. Choose STARTTLS (usually
   587) or implicit TLS (usually 465); both verify the certificate.
3. Save, then **Send test to me**. Tests work while delivery is disabled and are
   limited to one per minute. Enable delivery when the test arrives. Changes take
   effect without a restart.

The password is stored encrypted and never returned. Leave the field blank to
keep it; changing the server, port, TLS mode or username requires re-entering
it. For an unauthenticated relay, clear the username and choose **Remove saved
password**; no key is needed. If the key is lost, restore it or save the
password again. The console sends only registration and test emails; there is
no email password reset.

When registration is open, **Register** appears on the login page. An allowed
address receives a link to choose a password. Links expire after 30 minutes,
work once, and carry the token in the URL fragment; the server stores only its
hash and checks the allowlist again before creating the account. One request
per address per minute; a new link replaces the old one. The console sends at
most 30 emails per minute and holds at most 1,000 pending addresses. Responses
do not reveal whether an address is allowed or registered.

A configured OIDC provider can also register allowed addresses without SMTP when
its identity carries a verified email. Both methods create Members without team
access. Closing registration or removing an allowlist entry affects new accounts
only.

## Accounts and recovery

Sign-in uses FastAPI Users with Argon2 password hashes and revocable PostgreSQL
sessions. Session cookies are HTTPS, HttpOnly and SameSite Strict, and expire
after eight hours. Users change their password under **Your account**; for
accounts an administrator creates, share the initial password privately.
Password resets are done by an administrator.

Owners disable or reset any account; admins manage Member and Global viewer
accounts. Account changes revoke sessions, and the last active owner cannot be
demoted or disabled. Keep a second owner for recovery; the bootstrap command
never replaces existing accounts.

Accounts and sessions are in the PostgreSQL backup. To remove the console,
remove its route and service and keep the database; its tables can stay. For a
version rollback, follow the database recovery procedure; do not reverse
migrations by hand.

The console's application pool uses at most four connections and sixteen
waiting queries; its authentication pool uses two connections. Include both in
the deployment's PostgreSQL connection budget.

---

Title: Frequently asked questions
Canonical URL: https://ccimen.github.io/review-agent/docs/faq
Status: current
Last verified: 2026-11-17

# Frequently asked questions

## My organization already runs Review Agent. What does my team need to do?

Nothing to install. Comment `/review` on a pull request in a repository covered
by the organization's GitHub App installation. You need GitHub write or admin
permission, or a grant in the console's **Who can request reviews** list; see
[Who can request a review](./GITHUB_APP_PILOT.md#who-can-request-a-review). If
the repository is not enabled yet, a team maintainer can request it from the
team's **Repositories** tab in the [admin console](./ADMIN_PANEL.md). An
optional [`.review-agent/` package](./REPOSITORY_CONTEXT.md) adds team
instructions, architecture context, and accepted ADRs.

## Does it review automatically when a pull request opens?

No. Code review starts when an authorized user comments `/review`; comments from
bots, including GitHub Actions, are ignored. Comment `/review` again after
pushing fixes. Documentation review can run automatically when a team or
repository selects Automatic mode; see
[Documentation review](./DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md).

## Can another organization use our GitHub App?

Yes. Make the App public, have the other organization install it, and approve
that installation as an operator. Every installation shares the deployment's
database, job queue, and model route, unless a team has its own model
connection. See
[Share the App with other organizations](./GITHUB_APP_PILOT.md#share-the-app-with-other-organizations).

## How do I serve many repositories or a whole organization?

Deploy once, install the App on the organization, and approve the installation
once. Each repository the installation reaches is then enabled by its first
`/review` command; a review starts only if the commenter may request one. See
[Set up and share the GitHub App](./GITHUB_APP_PILOT.md), and
[scale workers](./DEPLOYMENT.md#scale-and-operate-the-queue) when queue wait
time grows.

## Is it a merge gate?

No. Reviews are advisory.

## Can it run contributor code?

No. The reviewer has no shell, browser, repository write access, delegation, or
code execution. It reads the pull request through bounded GitHub tools. See
[Security](./SECURITY.md).

## Does it use RAG or reranking?

The reviewer reads the diff and the files it asks for. The optional
[code graph](./CODE_GRAPH.md) is a retrieval path that returns up to ten
locations per query. Nothing reranks findings or context. See
[How reviews work](./HOW_REVIEWS_WORK.md).

## Does it find security problems?

Yes, within the pull request. The review procedure instructs the reviewer to
apply security-audit guidance to the changed code and to report vulnerabilities
and flawed security logic the pull request introduces or worsens. Those are
instructions to the model: code checks each finding it records, not that every
path was traced. It does not run exploits, query a CVE
database, audit unchanged code, or certify a repository as secure; keep
deterministic scanners in CI. See [How reviews work](./HOW_REVIEWS_WORK.md).

## Can it review architecture?

For the code a pull request changes, yes: rules implemented outside their owner,
duplicated policy, hidden coupling, and conflicts with accepted ADRs. Describe
the intended structure in the repository's
[`.review-agent/` package](./REPOSITORY_CONTEXT.md) so the review can check
against it. It does not assess the whole repository.

## Does feedback affect later reviews?

`/review false-positive` and `/review intentional` suppress the same finding in
later rounds while the code and ADR still match and the decision has not
expired (180 days for a comment). `/review feedback scope` and
`/review feedback missed` record evidence only. See
[Feedback and design decisions](./FEEDBACK_AND_DECISIONS.md).

## Can each repository have its own reviewer voice or rules?

Each repository can add review focus, communication preferences, technical
context, and accepted ADRs through its [`.review-agent/`
package](./REPOSITORY_CONTEXT.md), read from the pull request's base commit. The
deployment profile owns the reviewer's identity, procedure, and review rules
such as severity. Tools, authorization, the finding gates, and publication are
fixed in code, and neither a profile nor a repository can change them; see
[Behavior ownership](./BEHAVIOR_OWNERSHIP.md).

## What is stored in PostgreSQL?

Review runs, findings, coverage, publication state, human decisions, and
feedback. The database can contain unpublished findings and maintainer reasons,
so back it up and treat exports as sensitive. See [Security](./SECURITY.md).

## Why did a review fail or stop?

A request from an unauthorized requester or in a disabled repository is
rejected before a run exists: look for the delivery's `status=` and `reason=`
in the `review-github-app-worker` log
([failure codes](./OPERATIONS.md#failure-codes)). Once a run exists, common
causes are a stale head SHA or a GitHub permission failure; check the run's
failure code in the [Operations runbook](./OPERATIONS.md#runbook).

## Can we follow reviews in Slack or Microsoft Teams?

Review Agent publishes only to GitHub. GitHub's own apps can relay those
publications to a channel:

- Slack: `/github subscribe <owner>/<repo> reviews comments`
- Microsoft Teams: `@GitHub subscribe <owner>/<repo> reviews` (comments are on
  by default)

Code reviews arrive as comments and reviews. Documentation results that do not
change open findings appear only as a GitHub check, which these subscriptions
do not relay. Subscribe in a channel whose members can already read the
repository, because relayed comments contain review content. Starting a review
from Slack or Teams is not supported.

---

Title: Capabilities and limits
Canonical URL: https://ccimen.github.io/review-agent/docs/roadmap
Status: current
Last verified: 2026-11-17

# Capabilities and limits

## What it does

| Capability | Summary | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code review on request | `/review` reviews the pull request's current base and head commits and publishes advisory findings | [How reviews work](./HOW_REVIEWS_WORK.md) |
| Security review | The review procedure instructs the reviewer to trace untrusted input across trust boundaries in the changed code; code checks the findings it records, not the model's reasoning | [How reviews work](./HOW_REVIEWS_WORK.md#4-the-review) |
| Large pull requests | A pull request too large for one session can be reviewed in up to twelve parts that are merged into one review; files left unread are reported as incomplete coverage | [How reviews work](./HOW_REVIEWS_WORK.md#5-large-pull-requests) |
| Re-review and feedback | Earlier findings are re-checked; maintainers can mark a finding false positive or intentional | [Feedback and decisions](./FEEDBACK_AND_DECISIONS.md) |
| Repository context | A `.review-agent/` package adds instructions, platform context, and accepted design decisions | [Repository context](./REPOSITORY_CONTEXT.md) |
| Documentation review | `/review docs`, or an automatic mode, checks whether a pull request leaves mapped documents inaccurate | [Documentation review](./DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md) |
| Code graph (optional) | Structural and semantic lookups of related code | [Code graph](./CODE_GRAPH.md) |
| Admin console (optional) | Teams, roles, repository access, model connections, usage, audit, OIDC and SCIM | [Admin panel](./ADMIN_PANEL.md) |
| Many organizations | One deployment serves multiple approved GitHub App installations | [GitHub App setup](./GITHUB_APP_PILOT.md#share-the-app-with-other-organizations) |
| Deployment | One Compose stack for Docker, Dokploy, Coolify, and Portainer, and a Helm chart for Kubernetes | [Deployment](./DEPLOYMENT.md) |

State lives in one PostgreSQL database per environment. Jobs and publication
are lease-based, so workers and publishers can run in several replicas. An
interrupted review is retried from its stored job with a new model session,
within its attempt budget; an interrupted publication continues from its stored
parts ([durability](./HOW_REVIEWS_WORK.md#9-durability)).

## What it does not do

- **Block merges.** Reviews are advisory.
- **Start code reviews automatically.** A code review starts when an authorized
  user comments `/review`. Only documentation review has an automatic mode.
- **Review pull requests from forks.**
- **Run code.** Nothing from the pull request is executed, and no tests run.
- **Scan dependencies or the whole repository.** Keep CodeQL, dependency
  scanning, tests, and type checks in CI. Security review covers what the pull
  request changes.
- **Publish anywhere but GitHub.** GitHub's own Slack and Microsoft Teams apps
  can relay the comments; see the
  [FAQ](./FAQ.md#can-we-follow-reviews-in-slack-or-microsoft-teams).
- **Load a different reviewer profile per repository.** One deployment uses one
  profile; repositories customize through their `.review-agent/` package.

---

Title: Team access and model accounts
Canonical URL: https://ccimen.github.io/review-agent/docs/team-access-and-model-accounts
Status: current
Last verified: 2026-11-17

# Team access and model accounts

A team owns repositories, decides who in the console can see their reviews, and
can route those reviews to its own model account. Procedures are in the
[admin panel](ADMIN_PANEL.md) guide.

## Teams and repositories

A team is a named group of console accounts. An account can belong to several
teams, as **Maintainer** or **Viewer** in each. Platform owners and admins see
every team; global viewers can read every team; ordinary members see only their
own teams. A team the caller does not belong to returns `404`.

Each repository has at most one owning team:

- A maintainer requests a repository for the team. An owner or admin approves
  it, which checks the GitHub App grant, assigns the team and enables reviews in
  one step. Owners and admins can also assign, transfer or remove ownership
  directly.
- A transfer moves access to the repository's retained reviews to the new team.
- A repository without a team is visible only to owners, admins and global
  viewers, and its reviews use the deployment's default model route.

Team membership grants nothing on GitHub and does not decide
[who can request a review](GITHUB_APP_PILOT.md#who-can-request-a-review).

## What team members can do

| Action | Viewer | Maintainer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read the team's reviews, findings, quality reports, repositories and members | Yes | Yes |
| See the team's model connection and its account quota | Yes | Yes |
| Add, change or remove team members (existing active accounts, by exact email) | | Yes |
| Request repositories and withdraw requests | | Yes |
| Allow additional GitHub users to request reviews on a team repository | | Yes |
| Triage feedback and record finding decisions | | Yes |
| Retry or cancel the team's reviews | | Yes |
| Choose the team's model and reasoning effort from the allowed choices | | Yes |
| Connect, pause, enable or record the account of a team-owned connection | | Yes |

Only owners and admins approve repository requests, assign connections, set
team capacity, and read audit and usage reports. Membership changes take effect
on the next request.

## Model connections

A model connection is a Hermes runtime with its own provider credentials. Every
deployment has one shared connection. An owner can register more, each owned by
one team ([provision another connection](ADMIN_PANEL.md#provision-another-connection)).

When a review request is admitted, Review Agent resolves the route from the
repository's owning team:

1. **Connection:** the team's assigned connection, or the shared connection if
   none is assigned. An admin assigns it; a team-owned connection can serve only
   its own team.
2. **Model:** the team's chosen provider, model and reasoning effort, selected
   from the choices the connection allows. Without a team choice, the
   deployment's model from **Settings** (or its environment values before the
   first save).

The route is frozen into the request: later changes apply to new requests only,
queued reviews never switch account, and nothing falls back to another
connection or provider. A paused connection stops new dispatch.

## Limits

The team and connection caps count review jobs. A review is one job, except a
[split review](OPERATIONS.md#split-reviews), where each running part is one.

- **Team capacity:** at most four of a team's review jobs run at once by
  default, across all its connections. Admins can change the cap. The team
  recorded at admission is counted.
- **Connection capacity:** at most four review jobs per connection by default.
  Owners set it for the shared connection; owners and admins for a team-owned one.
- **Repository:** one review runs per repository at a time; the parts of that
  review may overlap.
- **Workers:** a job also needs a free worker slot
  ([queue rules](OPERATIONS.md#queue-rules)).
- **Fairness:** eligible teams take turns claiming work, with priority aging
  within each team.
- **Quota:** teams that share a connection share its Codex account quota, which
  also counts any other use of that account. When Codex reports the account
  exhausted, its queued reviews wait without using an attempt
  ([quota and concurrent reviews](ADMIN_PANEL.md#quota-and-concurrent-reviews)).

## Isolation

Team scope is access control inside one deployment and one database. All teams
share the same services, PostgreSQL database and job queue; the server filters
every query and action by team, and a dedicated connection keeps a team's
provider credentials and quota apart. It is not isolation between mutually
hostile tenants: owners, admins, global viewers and anyone with database access
can read every team's data. Use separate deployments where that boundary is
required.

---

Title: Operations
Canonical URL: https://ccimen.github.io/review-agent/docs/operations
Status: current
Last verified: 2026-11-18

# Operations

Day-two operation and recovery. First deployment, credentials and upgrades are
in [Deploy Review Agent](./DEPLOYMENT.md).

**Jump to:** [Runbook](#runbook) ·
[Diagnose a review run](#diagnose-a-review-run) ·
[Failure codes](#failure-codes) · [Backup and recovery](#backup-and-recovery) ·
[Configuration reference](#configuration-reference)

## Prerequisites

The [deployment guide](./DEPLOYMENT.md#deploy) covers Compose, Dokploy, Coolify
and Portainer. The public review route targets `review-admission:8644`.
Workers reach the private Hermes API on `8642`. PostgreSQL and Hermes stay off
the public network.

The deployment uses two named volumes:

| Volume | Mounted in | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hermes_review_data` | Profile installer and Hermes (read and write); workers (read-only) | Hermes config, provider credentials, sessions, managed skills, plugins, and the installed reviewer receipt. Admission derives the same contract from immutable image files and cannot read this volume. |
| `review_postgres_data` | `review-postgres` at `/var/lib/postgresql/data` | PostgreSQL review state. |

Do not run two Hermes gateways against the same `hermes_review_data` volume.

Two one-shot services run before the live services. `review-profile-install`
installs the selected managed profile under `/opt/data`. `review-db-migrate`
waits for PostgreSQL, applies checksum-verified schema migrations, and creates
or rotates the restricted runtime login. It is the only container that receives
both database URLs. Both finish as `Exited (0)`; inspect their logs when startup
stops. Manual recovery:

```bash
docker compose run --rm --no-deps review-profile-install
docker compose run --rm --no-deps review-db-migrate
docker compose exec hermes-review review-agent-admin database ready
```

### Profile

`REVIEW_AGENT_PROFILE` selects a trusted bundle key under `profiles/`;
the packaged default is `default-standard`. There are no aliases for earlier
profile names, and ADRs are read only from `.review-agent/decisions/`. The
installer rejects an unknown key before changing `HERMES_HOME`. A profile owns
`SOUL.md`, `workspace/AGENTS.md`, and the reviewed skills named in
`profile.json`; it cannot change model, route, tool, authorization, snapshot,
persistence, marker or lifecycle settings. Skill files are trusted,
code-reviewed content; `profile.json` validation does not make arbitrary skill
prose safe.

Keep the selected value in deployment configuration. Run outside Compose, the
installer reuses the last selected profile when neither the flag nor the
environment value is set. The installer replaces managed config, SOUL, AGENTS,
skills and plugin files from source control and records their digests with the
Hermes image, model, reasoning effort and tool-result budget. Admission stores
that contract with every review subject. A worker refuses queued work whose
contract differs from the installed one, and the developer is told to request a
fresh review.

### Database URLs

Use one database per environment. The example Compose network keeps PostgreSQL
private and uses separate credentials:

```text
REVIEW_AGENT_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://review_agent:<owner-password>@review-postgres:5432/review_agent
REVIEW_AGENT_RUNTIME_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://review_agent_runtime:<runtime-password>@review-postgres:5432/review_agent
```

Use the same URL-safe owner value for `REVIEW_AGENT_POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and the
first URL. Generate a different runtime value for the second URL. Hex output
from `openssl rand -hex 32` needs no percent-encoding.

## Connect the model provider

Inside the `hermes-review` container:

```bash
hermes plugins list
hermes model
/opt/review-agent-bootstrap/install.sh
```

Use Hermes' wizard to authenticate the provider selected by
`REVIEW_AGENT_MODEL_PROVIDER`. The default `openai-codex` route uses ChatGPT
device-code OAuth and needs no model API key. The only other supported
provider is `anthropic`; Hermes documents that Anthropic OAuth requires Claude
Max plus extra-usage credits, while its API-key route is independent. Rerunning the installer restores `REVIEW_AGENT_MODEL_PROVIDER`,
`REVIEW_AGENT_MODEL` and `REVIEW_AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT` after the wizard stores
credentials. `REVIEW_AGENT_MODEL` has no default; a deployment without it does
not start.

Once the console has saved settings, their model governs new reviews instead of
`REVIEW_AGENT_MODEL`; change it in **Settings**. A model changed there applies
to new requests, and queued reviews keep the route they were admitted with.

An environment change applies after the installer and services restart.
Rerunning the installer with a different provider, model or effort rewrites the
managed Hermes configuration, so reviews queued before it fail with
`review_contract_changed` and must be requested again. Verify:

```bash
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8642/health
hermes status
hermes doctor
hermes plugins list
```

Authentication and billing differ between providers. Use the
[Hermes provider guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/providers),
its [model catalog](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/model-catalog)
for model IDs, and its
[environment reference](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/environment-variables)
for API-key and custom-endpoint variables. A controlled review after deployment
is the final proof that the credential is entitled to the selected model.

## Health checks

```bash
review-agent-admin doctor
review-agent-admin queues inspect
```

`doctor` reports expired leases, review-capacity exhaustion, and work that has
been due for at least 90 seconds with neither a live worker nor a current lease.
Scheduled retries and quota waits do not trigger the missing-worker check. Dead
letters stay in the queue report as terminal history but do not consume
capacity or make `doctor` and dry-run smoke tests fail.

`doctor` reports `documentation_app` separately from core readiness. A missing
Checks permission or event subscription does not mark a working code-only
deployment unhealthy.

The console **Health** view shows due-work ages, capacity and quota waits, live
worker totals, and recent progress for each queue. **Activity** and
**Pull requests** show each request's recorded phase, scheduled retry or quota
check, and **Waiting for recovery** when a worker lease expires. There is no
completion percentage. Published results with incomplete or unknown coverage are
labeled **Incomplete**; their finding count is not a clean result. GitHub
receives only the final result or failure notice; these reports do not change
GitHub checks or merge requirements.

## GitHub trigger

The App delivers these events to `/webhooks/github-app`:

- `issue_comment`: `/review` and feedback commands;
- `pull_request` and `check_run`: automatic documentation review and its
  re-runs;
- `installation` and `installation_repositories`: the repository inventory.

Admission stores the signed delivery before any provider read. For `/review`
and feedback commands, the App worker then checks, through the private
gateway, the repository's enabled state and the sender's current access
([who can request a review](./GITHUB_APP_PILOT.md#who-can-request-a-review)).
How a command enables a repository in automatic mode, and how 0.5.0-rc.1 and
earlier differ, is under
[automatic activation](./GITHUB_APP_PILOT.md#automatic-approve-once). For
feedback, the gateway also
rechecks the open pull request before anything is recorded. Automatic
documentation reviews have no sender check.

Installation webhooks and inventory sync record repositories but never enable
one. [Approve the installation](./GITHUB_APP_PILOT.md#4-approve-the-installation)
explains how a repository is enabled in each mode.

Set `REVIEW_AGENT_FEEDBACK_ENABLED=true` to show the copyable feedback commands
in the review comment.

## Run a review

On an open pull request, including a draft, an authorized user comments:

```text
/review
```

Each `/review` after the previous run reaches a terminal state starts a new
round (`Review 2`, ...), including a rerun of the same base and head. A second
`/review` on the same pull request while a run is active is a duplicate.
Pull requests in different repositories run concurrently; one repository runs
one review at a time. Applying a native suggestion does not
mark its finding resolved; run CI and post a new `/review`. Review mechanics are
in [How reviews work](./HOW_REVIEWS_WORK.md).

## Developer feedback

The feedback commands and what each records are in
[Feedback and design decisions](./FEEDBACK_AND_DECISIONS.md).

## Runbook

### Queue

```bash
review-agent-admin queues inspect
review-agent-admin jobs list --limit 100
```

`queues inspect` reports webhook intake, review jobs and publication delivery
from the same reader the console uses. Publication counts include final review
comments and pending failure notices.

| Signal | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `waiting`, `due`, `delayed` | Waiting work, split by whether its scheduled availability has arrived. Due work may still need a scheduler slot. |
| `oldest_due_age_seconds` | Time since the oldest waiting item became due, excluding its scheduled delay. |
| `oldest_waiting_age_seconds` | Total waiting age; for publications, delivery lag since generation. |
| `next_available_at` | The next scheduled retry or cooldown expiry that makes delayed work due. |
| `live_workers`, `worker_capacity` | Recently reporting worker instances and their advertised capacity, using the returned `worker_stale_after_seconds` threshold. |
| `leased`, `expired_leases` | Claimed work and the subset whose lease expired. |
| `capacity_waiting` | Webhook requests deferred by the last admission capacity check. |
| `cooldown_waiting`, `cooldown_until` | Review jobs waiting for model-account quota and the next quota deadline. GitHub retry deadlines are included in `next_available_at`. |
| `last_progress_at`, `last_heartbeat_at` | The latest persisted start or completion, and the latest heartbeat of leased work. A heartbeat proves liveness, not completion. |
| `last_terminal_reason`, `last_terminal_at` | The latest terminal reason and its time, including rejected webhook requests. |

Idle queues have zero waiting and leased counts and null wait ages.

Release a delayed queued retry, or cancel a job's active run:

```bash
review-agent-admin jobs retry JOB_ID
review-agent-admin jobs cancel JOB_ID
```

`jobs retry` cannot revive failed or dead-letter work: inspect the failure, fix
its cause, and post a new `/review`. `jobs cancel` fences a leased worker by
failing the owning run and reconciling its job in one transaction; it also
retires a publication waiting on a GitHub cooldown.

### Runs

```bash
review-agent-memory runs --repo OWNER/REPOSITORY --limit 10
review-agent-memory runs --repo OWNER/REPOSITORY --stats
review-agent-memory runs --repo OWNER/REPOSITORY --pr PR_NUMBER --limit 10
review-agent-memory runs --repo OWNER/REPOSITORY --pr PR_NUMBER --stats
```

`--stats` also counts terminal runs by `failure_code`, failed attempts by cause,
and the tokens of attempts that reported usage beside the number of attempts
started. `runs --failed` shows failure-status delivery state, attempt count,
maximum attempts and the last delivery failure.

A healthy run moves through `accepted`, `fetching_pr`, `collecting_diff`,
`reviewing`, `rendering`, `publishing` and `posted`.

### Diagnose a review run

```bash
review-agent-memory runs --run-id RUN_ID
```

The JSON report is printed on standard output and covers one run:

- status, `failure_code` and `failure_detail`;
- the requested provider, model and reasoning effort;
- each job (the main job and any parts) with its attempts and lease generation;
- the newest 100 attempts, with their tokens and why each ended;
- part progress and coverage counts, with at most 20 unavailable and 20
  truncated paths.

It contains no review text, comment bodies or requester identities, and stays
under 512 KiB so a tool that can only read container files can open it. For
such a tool, redirect the output to a file; no report directory exists until you
create one, for example with `mkdir -p /opt/data/review-memory` in
`hermes-review`.

`failure_detail` is at most 300 characters: one of the reviewer's own messages
or Hermes error text, which Hermes redacts. Treat it as untrusted text. When
retries run out, the run's `failure_detail` repeats the last attempt's cause.

Hermes retries each model call up to `agent.api_max_retries` times (8 in the
managed `config.yaml`) with backoff from 2 to 60 seconds, which rides out a
provider overload of about 3 to 4.5 minutes before the turn fails and the worker
schedules a new attempt.

Inspect coverage and publication:

```bash
review-agent-memory coverage --run-id RUN_ID
review-agent-memory publications --repo OWNER/REPOSITORY --pr PR_NUMBER
```

A GitHub comment POST can succeed even when its response reports a transient
failure. Before retrying, the publisher looks for a recent comment with the same
App author, publication marker, part number and body, including on its last
attempt. If delivery cannot be confirmed, the failure status warns that review
comments may already exist; check GitHub before requesting another review.

### Stalled runs

After a crash, mark stale runs failed. The publisher then claims and delivers
their failure statuses:

```bash
review-agent-memory runs --mark-stalled --stale-after-minutes 10 --repo OWNER/REPOSITORY --pr PR_NUMBER
```

The publisher leases each failure status from PostgreSQL, recovers an existing
marker after a crash, retries transient GitHub failures, and stops after the
stored attempt limit. A later review of the same pull request suppresses
obsolete status work. A closed or merged pull request gets no new failure
status; one already posted before the close is kept, not edited. Manual recovery
reopens an exhausted status with a fresh attempt budget.

### Failure codes

Review run attempts (`failure_code`):

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `hermes_agent_error` | Hermes ended the turn early, for example after its model-call retries ran out during a provider overload. |
| `hermes_output_truncated` | The model's output was cut off. |
| `review_not_terminal` | The turn ended before the review recorded a terminal state. |
| `hermes_http_<status>` | Hermes answered with that HTTP status. |
| `hermes_timeout`, `hermes_unreachable` | The worker's request to Hermes timed out or could not connect. |
| `source_unavailable`, `preflight_rejected` | Review source checks failed before the model ran. |

Run and publication states:

| Symptom | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `running` with an old heartbeat, or `stalled` | Execution stopped before a terminal state. Mark stale runs failed before retrying. |
| `publish_failed` | GitHub publication was attempted and failed; inspect `failure=`. |
| `body_too_large` | The review could not fit within the per-comment byte budget. |
| `review_contract_changed` | The installed reviewer changed after the review was queued: the profile, skill or plugin bundle (an upgrade), or the managed Hermes configuration (the installer rerun with a different provider, model or effort). A model changed in console **Settings** does not cause this; queued reviews keep their route. Make every service run the same release and installed configuration, then request a fresh review. |
| `stale` | The pull request base or head changed before posting. |
| `pr_not_open` | The pull request was closed or merged during the review. The run stops at its next tool call without a retry or failure comment. |
| `finding_decisions_changed` | A human decision on one of the findings changed while the publication waited. Feedback on the same finding identity in another pull request also counts. Request a fresh `/review`. |
| `finding_groups_changed` | A newer review published its finding groups while this older write was in flight. The newer groups stay current. |

A failed or stale publication never activates its proposed groups, but a comment
already sent to GitHub may still be visible.

Admission (App worker log `status=` and `reason=`):

| Reason | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `review_waiting_for_capacity` | `status=received`. The active-job limit is reached; the request is retried every `REVIEW_AGENT_GITHUB_APP_CAPACITY_RETRY_SECONDS` without using processing attempts, rechecking authorization and the pull request each time. |
| `review_admission_busy` | Lock contention; uses the normal bounded processing-attempt budget. |
| `review_admission_expired` | `status=failed`. The request waited longer than `REVIEW_AGENT_GITHUB_APP_ADMISSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`. After fixing capacity or worker availability, post a new `/review`; redelivering the same webhook GUID does not reopen it. |

An expired request leaves a terminal delivery receipt. Code-review receipts
erase their normalized payload; documentation receipts keep their bounded event
envelope until explicit pruning.

GitHub gateway errors name the endpoint, for example
`github_403_get_pull_request`, `github_403_list_issue_comments`,
`github_403_create_issue_comment` or `github_403_create_pull_request_review`.
They identify a missing App permission or an organization approval. The token
scopes are in [Security model](./SECURITY.md#github-credential-boundaries).

`review-agent-memory` errors (one bounded JSON object on standard error, never
the original exception message; argument parsing errors keep argparse usage
output and exit `2`):

| Error code | Retry? | Exit | Operator action |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `invalid_command_input` | no | 64 | Correct the requested limit or argument. |
| `command_rejected` or `database_operation_failed` | no | 65 | Correct the requested scope; check application health for a database failure. |
| `internal_error` | no | 70 | Report the included exception type. |
| `artifact_io_failed` | no | 74 | Repair the private file path or permissions. |
| `database_unavailable` or `database_busy` | yes | 75 | Retry after PostgreSQL connectivity or contention recovers. |
| `invalid_configuration` or `database_not_ready` | no | 78 | Correct configuration or complete the database migration and readiness steps. |

## Capacity and scaling

Scaling procedures and examples are in
[Scale and operate the queue](./DEPLOYMENT.md#scale-and-operate-the-queue).

### Queue rules

- Worker slots = `review-worker` replicas × `REVIEW_AGENT_WORKER_CONCURRENCY`.
  Each slot runs one review job; a split review uses one per running part. A
  worker claims only when a slot is free and the job's model connection, team
  and repository [limits](./TEAM_ACCESS_AND_MODEL_ACCOUNTS.md#limits) allow it.
- `REVIEW_AGENT_ACTIVE_JOB_LIMIT` bounds queued, leased and
  publication-waiting reviews. At the limit, the App worker keeps the accepted
  request and retries admission without using processing attempts. Each retry
  reauthorizes through GitHub; the default 300 seconds is about 24 permission
  and snapshot reads per hour per waiting review, plus token exchanges.
- Keep `REVIEW_AGENT_JOB_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS` below half of
  `REVIEW_AGENT_JOB_LEASE_SECONDS`.
- Changing `REVIEW_AGENT_GITHUB_APP_ADMISSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` applies to
  pending requests.

### GitHub rate limits

GitHub cooldowns keep the `Retry-After` deadline (seconds or HTTP date) and,
when the remaining quota is zero, the `X-RateLimit-Reset` time. Admission,
publication and failure-status retries wait until both the provider deadline and
the normal retry delay have passed. PostgreSQL stores that time, so a restart or
explicit retry cannot bypass it.

- Waiting uses no attempts; failed calls still use the attempt budget.
- A rate limit without usable timing waits at least one minute. A transient
  error without usable timing keeps the normal transport retry.
- Review admission still expires at its age limit, without another GitHub call,
  even if the provider deadline is later. Valid provider deadlines are never
  shortened.
- A newer successful review suppresses an older pending failure status, even in
  cooldown. Feedback acknowledgements honor the provider deadline and have no
  separate age limit. Permanent denials stay terminal.

### Database connections

Plan the maximum pool capacity against the PostgreSQL connection limit:

```text
review-worker replicas × (REVIEW_AGENT_WORKER_CONCURRENCY + 1)
+ review-github-app-worker replicas × 2
+ review-publisher replicas × 2
+ review-admission replicas × 4
+ review-github-gateway replicas × 4
+ hermes-review replicas × 4
+ review-admin replicas × 6 (four application and two authentication connections)
+ operator command processes × 4 (normally one in use)
```

Pools open connections on demand. Keep the total below the database limit with
headroom for maintenance and monitoring. The bundled database allows
`REVIEW_AGENT_POSTGRES_MAX_CONNECTIONS` (default 200); an external database owns
its own limit.

### Worker termination and lease recovery

`SIGTERM` stops a worker from claiming more work. A job that has not yet started
its Hermes request goes back to the queue without using an attempt. A review
already running continues and keeps heartbeating until it finishes or the
platform force-terminates the process after
`REVIEW_AGENT_WORKER_TERMINATION_GRACE_SECONDS`; the worker never writes a
guessed terminal state.

After termination, the last heartbeat stands until its lease expires. Another
worker then requeues the job with a new lease generation, or dead-letters it when
attempts are exhausted. With PostgreSQL healthy, at least one worker alive and
no recovery backlog, the bound from `SIGTERM` to requeue is:

```text
termination grace + lease duration + recovery interval
```

With the defaults, `150 + 120 + 30 = 300 seconds`; from the force-termination
point, 150 seconds. The old Hermes session may still finish upstream, but the
generation fence rejects its late writes. Never shorten recovery by releasing a
lease while that model call can still run.

### Review limits

The reviewer has no repository-size quota. It reads in bounded pages and
reports incomplete coverage when one of these boundaries stops it:

| Boundary | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Changed files | GitHub lists at most 3,000 files per pull request. If even a one-file page exceeds the response budget, registration stays incomplete. |
| Source files | Read in line pages at the exact revision. Files above 1 MB use the raw Contents response up to a 2 MB per-request memory guard; larger or binary files cannot be read as source. A failed source read does not change diff coverage, which counts only the diffs returned. A source page carries at most 400 lines. |
| Patches GitHub omits | For an added UTF-8 file up to 1 MB, the gateway builds the patch from head content, up to 200,000 characters. Otherwise the file's diff stays incomplete. |
| Tool results | `plugins.entries.review-agent-tools.settings.result_max_chars` (default 160,000), further held to the Hermes per-result and per-response limits for the session's model (100,000 and 200,000 characters for windows of 166,667 tokens or more). A single-path diff or source page holds at most a seventh of the per-result limit. A batched diff result holds at most a fifth of the smaller of `result_max_chars` and the per-response limit (32,000 by default); one diff call accepts up to 50 paths, and the review procedure allows at most four batch calls in one model response. |
| Historical context | 200 paths per call. |
| Findings | 200 per atomic record; more rejects the record. At most 12 native suggestions per round. |
| Publication | `REVIEW_AGENT_PUBLISH_MAX_BYTES` (65,000 UTF-8 bytes per comment part, including framing and metadata). Larger reviews are split into continuation comments. |
| Diff cache | At most 16 snapshots and 32 MiB per tool process; eviction causes a fresh read, never a skipped file. Debug logs from `hermes_plugins.review_agent_tools.review.diff_cache` report hits and oversized snapshots without source content. |

An INFO log from `hermes_plugins.review_agent_tools.tools.source` reports
`Java guidance returned` with the run ID and profile digest when the Java
companion is delivered. It confirms delivery to the model, not that every check
was applied.

The managed configuration does not set `agent.max_turns` or
`context_file_max_chars`; Hermes runs turns to completion and derives the
context-file allowance from the model's window. See the upstream
[Hermes configuration](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/configuration).

### Split reviews

A code review is reviewed in parts when its changed files, not counting any
file whose own diff exceeds the largest part, together exceed the largest part;
[Large pull requests](./HOW_REVIEWS_WORK.md#5-large-pull-requests)
describes how. Documentation reviews are never split.

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| A review is split when | the diffs that each fit the largest part together exceed it |
| Preferred part | about half the context window: about 372,000 diff characters at 500,000 tokens, 192,000 at 272,000 |
| Largest part | below the compression threshold: about 608,000 diff characters at 500,000 tokens, 321,000 at 272,000 |
| Parts in one review | at most 12 |
| Jobs of one review that run at once | at most 3, and at most the model connection's concurrency minus one, but never fewer than 1 |
| Report one part hands in | the smaller of `result_max_chars` and the per-response limit, divided by the review's number of parts plus one, and at most the per-result limit. By default, with 160,000 as that smaller value: 40,000 serialized characters in a three-part review, 12,307 in a twelve-part one |
| Changed file without a GitHub patch | counted as 48 characters per changed line |

Cost and accounting:

- A split review runs one short registration session, one session per part, and
  one final session. Model usage grows with the diff.
- Each part counts as one review job against the model connection's and the
  team's concurrency limits and waits for model quota like any review.
- A part that uses up `REVIEW_AGENT_JOB_MAX_ATTEMPTS` fails the whole review;
  nothing partial is published.
- The console shows a split review as one request with usage summed over its
  parts. `review-agent-admin jobs list` names each job's `part`; `0` is the main
  job. Queue health does not count a main job waiting for its parts as waiting
  or due work.
- In a split review, a file whose own diff exceeds the largest part, and files
  after the twelfth part, are assigned to no part; left unread, they appear in
  the coverage details. When the other files fit one part, the review is not
  split and its single session reads such a file as far as it gets. The gateway
  log records each session's window and each split's part sizes.

## Documentation review operation

[Documentation review](DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md) covers manual requests,
automatic opt-in, scope and results. The deployment switch in console
**Settings** defaults off. Team defaults and repository overrides keep their
modes while the deployment switch is off. Changing a team default to Off does not
override an explicit Automatic repository setting.

To stop documentation spending, turn off the deployment switch; for a narrower
stop, set a repository to Off or back to inheritance. Retained results and usage
stay available. The repository console checks the stored installation grant and
offers an exact-revision configuration **Refresh**; neither grants GitHub access
or runs a model.

## Database access and retention

The migration owner is available only to the one-shot database job. It must own
the application schema, have `CREATEROLE`, and be able to grant `CONNECT` on the
target database; it does not need superuser. Live services use the shared
runtime login, which can read and write application tables and sequences but
cannot change the schema or migration ledger.

`database prepare` is idempotent. It checks the effective connection
parameters, applies migrations, and creates or rotates one marked runtime role.
It refuses to adopt an unrelated or privilege-expanded role with the same name,
and finishes by connecting as the runtime login:

```bash
review-agent-admin database prepare
review-agent-admin database ready
```

To rotate the runtime password, update `REVIEW_AGENT_RUNTIME_DATABASE_URL`, run
the one-shot database job with both URLs available, and restart the live
services. To roll back, put the previous password back, run `database prepare`
again, and restart. Existing connections stay valid until they reconnect, so do
either as one maintenance operation. Never give the migration-owner URL to a
live service.

### Retention ownership

Durable history is kept unless this table says otherwise:

| Tables | Owner | Default and exemption |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_migrations` | Release operator | Permanent checksum ledger; never edit or prune. |
| `github_app_installations`, `github_app_repository_access`, `github_app_installation_events`, `github_app_repository_access_events` | Platform operator | Preserve current authorization and its audit history. |
| `github_webhook_deliveries` | Platform operator | Preserve active deliveries. Old terminal `accepted`, `ignored`, `rejected` and `failed` receipts may be pruned only with the bounded command below. |
| `repositories`, `pull_requests`, `review_subjects`, `review_runs`, `review_jobs`, `review_parts`, `review_run_files`, `review_file_reads`, `review_decision_snapshots`, `review_guidance_snapshots` | Repository owner | Preserve review identity, coverage, lifecycle, and the guidance and decision context each run used. |
| `model_executions`, `review_attempt_usage`, `review_attempt_failures` | Platform operator | Preserve each attempt's model account, token usage and failure cause; usage reports and run diagnostics read them. |
| `review_dispatch_turns` | Platform operator | Scheduling state: one row per team with its last claim time. Not history. |
| `worker_instances`, `worker_events` | Platform operator | Liveness only. Workers delete instances not seen for seven days and keep the newest 1,000 events per worker. |
| `documentation_reviews`, `documentation_admissions` | Repository owner | Preserve exact scope, evidence, results and admission provenance with review history. |
| `repository_documentation_configuration` | Repository maintainer | Keep the latest configuration inspection; a later Refresh replaces it. Display state, not review authority. |
| `finding_identities`, `finding_occurrences`, `finding_suggestions`, `finding_decisions`, `intentional_design_evidence`, `decision_audit`, `pull_request_finding_references`, `pull_request_finding_groups`, `finding_group_changes` | Repository owner | Preserve finding history, grouping and human decisions. |
| `publications`, `publication_parts`, `publication_findings` | Repository owner | Preserve exact publication and recovery evidence. |
| `admin_users`, `admin_sessions` | Deployment owner | Preserve console accounts and revocable sessions; treat backups as credential-bearing data. |
| `admin_registration_policy`, `admin_email_settings` | Deployment owner | Preserve the registration policy and email delivery settings. The SMTP password is stored encrypted with `REVIEW_AGENT_EMAIL_SECRET_KEY`. |
| `admin_registration_requests` | Deployment owner | Short-lived: a pending email registration holds the email address, a digest of the emailed token and a 30-minute expiry. Completing the registration deletes it; an expired row stays until a later accepted registration request removes expired rows. |
| `admin_oidc_requests` | Deployment owner | Short-lived and credential-bearing: an organization sign-in in progress holds digests of its state and browser values, the nonce and the PKCE code verifier in clear, a five-minute expiry and, while a signed-in user links an account, that user's session token. The callback deletes it; an abandoned row stays until a later sign-in that is started successfully removes expired rows, or until the linked user or session is deleted. |
| `teams`, `team_members`, `team_repositories`, `repository_requests`, `repository_review_requesters` | Deployment owner | Preserve team access, repository ownership, request decisions and requester grants. A removed requester grant is deleted. |
| `model_connections`, `model_accounts`, `team_model_policies`, `model_login_sessions` | Deployment owner | Preserve model connection registrations, the account bound to each, team routing and the record of console sign-in attempts. Provider credentials are not stored here; they live on the Hermes volume. |
| `integrations`, `integration_teams` | Deployment owner | Preserve application integrations and their team scope, including revoked ones. Only a digest of each credential is stored. |
| `deployment_settings`, `service_settings_loads` | Deployment owner | Preserve every saved settings revision. `service_settings_loads` gains one row per service start and is not pruned. |
| `admin_run_actions` | Deployment owner | Preserve who retried, cancelled or marked a run stalled, and why. |
| `admin_audit_events` | Deployment owner | Preserve access changes and human audit evidence. Successful application read receipts can be pruned only with the bounded integration command below. |
| `review_quality_feedback`, `review_quality_feedback_triage`, `processed_feedback_events` | Quality owner | Preserve feedback, triage and idempotency receipts. |
| `coach_runs`, `coach_candidates`, `coach_intervention_outcomes` | None | No longer read or written. This release keeps the tables and their rows. Whether an earlier release can run against the current schema is decided as the [rollback boundary](./DEPLOYMENT.md#rollback-boundary) describes. |
| `verification_runs`, `candidate_verifications`, `candidate_reconciliations` | None | No longer read or written. This release keeps the tables and their rows; the same [rollback boundary](./DEPLOYMENT.md#rollback-boundary) applies. |

Raw webhook bodies are not stored. Terminal documentation deliveries keep their
bounded normalized event envelope until the pruning command removes the
delivery; the admitted run keeps its own provenance receipt.

Preview terminal webhook history before a cutoff. The limit is also capped by
`REVIEW_AGENT_OPERATOR_PAGE_MAX_ITEMS`:

```bash
review-agent-admin database prune-webhook-deliveries \
  --before 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z \
  --limit 100 \
  --actor "operator:alice" \
  --reason "approved retention window"
```

The JSON receipt reports the matched rows, oldest processed timestamp, and
whether more rows remain. Take and verify a backup, then repeat the command with
`--apply`. Each apply deletes one oldest-first batch; concurrent applies
serialize, so `more` stays accurate. Active deliveries and other tables are
untouched.

Every successful application report read appends an audit event. Review Agent
does not delete these automatically; choose a retention window and cleanup
cadence before enabling scheduled reports. Preview one batch:

```bash
review-agent-admin database prune-integration-reads \
  --before 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z \
  --limit 100 \
  --actor "operator:alice" \
  --reason "approved application read retention window"
```

The receipt identifies `integration_reads` and reports `oldest_recorded_at`.
Only successful `integration_read` events before the cutoff are eligible;
credential creation and revocation, failed reads, human audit events and newer
receipts are kept. Keep any required export or verified backup, then apply with
`--apply`. Each invocation deletes at most one batch; `more: true` means another
remains. Save each CLI receipt with the deployment's maintenance records, and
schedule repeated runs through existing maintenance tooling.

## Backup and recovery

PostgreSQL may contain unpublished findings and human-entered reasons; store
backups securely. Back up the database the application uses: the commands in
this section are for the bundled `review-postgres` service and its
`review_agent` database. When `REVIEW_AGENT_DATABASE_URL` names another host or
database, run `pg_dump` and `pg_restore` with the same options against that
database from a host with the PostgreSQL client tools; a dump of an unused
local volume is not a backup.

Create a logical backup from the Compose host. Each backup gets its own file,
and the shell refuses to write over an existing one, so neither a failed dump
nor a second backup started in the same second replaces an archive:

```bash
dump="review-agent-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).dump"
( umask 077; set -o noclobber
  docker compose exec -T review-postgres \
    pg_dump --username=review_agent --dbname=review_agent --format=custom \
    > "$dump" ) && echo "Backup written: $dump"
```

Without the last line's message the dump failed; a file it left is incomplete.
Keep the previous verified archive until the new one has passed the restore
test below.

Test recovery in a fresh database before relying on a backup. The archive
records the grants to the runtime role, including its default privileges, but
not the role: PostgreSQL roles belong to the cluster, not to a database. In a
cluster without that role, `pg_restore --exit-on-error` alone stops at the
first grant. Restore without ownership and grants, connected as the migration
owner, and let `database prepare` create the runtime role and its grants.

- **Restore test on the production cluster:** no service has to stop. Restore
  into a new temporary database, check it, and drop it. `$dump` is the archive
  to test. Each step runs only if the one before it succeeded:

  ```bash
  target="review_agent_restore_test_$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"
  docker compose exec -T review-postgres \
    createdb --username=review_agent "$target" &&
  docker compose exec -T review-postgres \
    pg_restore --username=review_agent --dbname="$target" \
    --no-owner --no-privileges --exit-on-error < "$dump" &&
  docker compose exec -T review-postgres \
    psql --username=review_agent --dbname="$target" --set ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
    --command "SELECT (SELECT max(version) FROM review_agent.schema_migrations) AS schema_version, (SELECT max(id) FROM review_agent.review_runs) AS latest_run" &&
  docker compose exec -T review-postgres \
    dropdb --username=review_agent "$target" &&
  echo "Restore test passed: $dump"
  ```

  Without the final message a step failed. The temporary database, if it was
  created, is left for inspection; drop it by its name afterwards. Compare
  `latest_run` with a review you know was the most recent when the backup was
  taken, for example from **Review history** or `review-agent-admin jobs list`:
  a restore of the wrong or an empty database passes every other step. Copying
  grants would give the runtime role access to another database, which
  `database prepare` rejects.
- **Production recovery into a separate cluster:** stop every service that
  reads or writes Review Agent state. Run the commands with every Compose file
  the deployment uses, so that `review-admin` and the other overlay services
  are included. The second command lists every container of the project with
  its state; every service other than `review-postgres` must show `exited`. A
  container that is `restarting` has not stopped. Stop anything outside this
  project that uses the same database as well:

  ```bash
  docker compose stop $(docker compose config --services | grep -vx review-postgres)
  docker compose ps --all --format '{{.Service}} {{.State}}'
  ```

  In the new cluster, create the migration-owner role and an empty database it
  owns. The bundled `review-postgres` creates both when it first starts on an
  empty volume; start only that service, because the restore needs the database
  as it is before `review-db-migrate` has run. Restore as the migration owner,
  then set `REVIEW_AGENT_DATABASE_URL` and `REVIEW_AGENT_RUNTIME_DATABASE_URL`
  to the restored database and run the one-shot database job, the only
  container with both URLs. It runs `database prepare`, which applies pending
  migrations, creates the runtime role and its grants, and connects once as
  the runtime login:

  Run these in the Compose project of the new cluster, with `$dump` naming a
  verified archive. The migration job runs only if the restore succeeded:

  ```bash
  docker compose up -d --wait review-postgres &&
  docker compose exec -T review-postgres \
    pg_restore --username=review_agent --dbname=review_agent \
    --no-owner --no-privileges --exit-on-error < "$dump" &&
  docker compose run --rm --no-deps review-db-migrate &&
  echo "Restored and prepared"
  ```

  For an external database, run the same `pg_restore` options from a host with
  the PostgreSQL client tools. A successful `database prepare` proves the
  schema and the runtime login, not that the data came back: it also succeeds
  on an empty database. Check the data before any other service starts,
  because a restored publisher or worker continues pending work as soon as it
  runs:

  ```bash
  docker compose exec -T review-postgres \
    psql --username=review_agent --dbname=review_agent --set ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
    --command "SELECT id, status, started_at FROM review_agent.review_runs ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5"
  ```

  The rows must include the reviews you know existed before the backup. Only
  then redeploy, and run `review-agent-admin database ready` and
  `review-agent-admin doctor` in `hermes-review`, where the database URL is the
  runtime login.

Some migrations change the schema in ways older images cannot read (for
example 016, 029 and 037); older images must not run against the migrated
schema. Before such an
upgrade, drain admission, active reviews and publications, stop every
application service including `review-admin`, and deploy all services from the
same revision. Rolling back requires the pre-upgrade backup with its matching
images; never remove columns or reverse a migration in place.

## Updating and validation

Upgrade through the [deployment procedure](DEPLOYMENT.md#upgrade-and-roll-back-production).
On redeploy, `review-profile-install` refreshes the managed profile and
`review-db-migrate` verifies and applies migrations before the gateway starts.

`HERMES_IMAGE` is pinned to a Hermes release tag and its immutable digest. Change
it only through a reviewed dependency update, never to a moving `latest` or
`main` tag. The main image keeps the Python version that Hermes supports; the
pins are listed in
[RELEASING.md](https://github.com/CCimen/review-agent/blob/main/RELEASING.md#runtime-dependency-pins).

## Quality report and triage

Run these in the `hermes-review` container.

1. **Weekly quality report.**

   ```bash
   review-agent-memory quality --days 30
   review-agent-memory quality --days 30 --repo OWNER/REPOSITORY --json
   ```

   It shows false positives beside published findings, scope and missed-issue
   feedback beside completed reviews, coverage, the triage backlog (regardless
   of the activity window), and cohorts by repository, profile, review
   contract, provider, model, and policy revision. Compare like-for-like
   cohorts, do not read missing feedback as accuracy, and do not rank
   developers or repositories from the counts.

2. **Triage missed issues.** Only an operator classifies one; a coding agent
   may prepare the evidence but must not choose the status or owner. In the
   console, a team maintainer or platform admin uses **Review quality**
   ([run actions](./ADMIN_PANEL.md#review-history-and-run-actions)). Without
   the console, find the feedback ID in an [export](#offline-operator-tools)
   (table `review_quality_feedback`). The export is private: do not give it to
   a coding agent or paste it into model context, and delete it after triage.
   Then append a state:

   ```bash
   review-agent-memory triage-feedback FEEDBACK_ID \
     --status actionable \
     --stable-key review-rule.auth-boundary \
     --target-owner review_rule \
     --actor "github:OPERATOR" \
     --reason "Two independent reviews missed the same authorization boundary."
   ```

   Statuses are `pending`, `actionable`, `duplicate`, `insufficient`, and
   `resolved`. Only `actionable` takes `--stable-key` (lowercase) and one
   `--target-owner`: `source_tool`, `coverage`, `review_rule`, `profile`,
   `repository_decision`, or `documentation`. Triage is append-only: the
   latest state counts, and a later `resolved`, `duplicate`, or `insufficient`
   removes the item from the actionable count without deleting its history.

3. **Change the owner.** Change an actionable item's owner (profile, rule,
   tool, or repository context) through a normal pull request. Never run
   Hermes `/learn` in the live reviewer profile.

List, show and decide findings:

```bash
review-agent-memory list --repo OWNER/REPOSITORY
review-agent-memory show FINGERPRINT_PREFIX --repo OWNER/REPOSITORY

review-agent-memory decide FINGERPRINT false_positive \
  --repo OWNER/REPOSITORY \
  --pr PR_NUMBER \
  --local-reference F2 \
  --actor "github:alice" \
  --reason "The scope-checked repository binds resource_scope_id before this query." \
  --expires-days 180

review-agent-memory decide FINGERPRINT resolved \
  --repo OWNER/REPOSITORY \
  --pr PR_NUMBER \
  --local-reference F2 \
  --actor "github:alice" \
  --reason "Fixed in the latest commit."
```

Other decision values are `accepted_risk`, `duplicate` and `reopen`. Prefer
exact observation IDs or pull-request references (`F2`). Suppression trust rules
are in [Security model](SECURITY.md#human-governed-suppressions).

## Offline operator tools

`export` runs outside the live review path. It reads PostgreSQL and writes one
repository's review history as a private JSON file for an operator, at most
`--row-limit` rows per table (capped by
`REVIEW_AGENT_OPERATOR_EXPORT_MAX_ROWS`). The webhook reviewer never reads the
file, and it publishes nothing. An export can contain maintainer-entered
reasons or repository text; scrub it before committing or sharing, and never
paste a raw database export into a model.

```bash
review-agent-memory export \
  --repo OWNER/REPOSITORY \
  --row-limit ROW_LIMIT \
  --output /opt/data/private-review/export.json
```

## Configuration reference

Every variable the Compose files interpolate. **Required** variables stop
`docker compose` when unset. Settings saved in the admin console override the
corresponding environment defaults; see
[Environment defaults and admin controls](./ADMIN_PANEL.md#environment-defaults-and-admin-controls).
Services read these values at startup.
